intro.t: You've compared the photos. Now answer the question, properly, with a reason. Six ways to give a real answer.

close.t: Excellent. Compare, then answer, with a reason. That's a complete Part 2.

reels.note: Answers "why" with a reason straight away.

ex.t: {I suppose it's because} the cinema is a treat, and games are free.
ex.q: Compare the two photographs and say why the people might have chosen to spend their time in these ways.
ex.scene: Photo 1: People watching a film in a cinema · Photo 2: A family playing a board game together at home

ex.t: {I suppose it's because} they love nature and want some peace.
ex.q: Compare the two photographs and say why the people might have decided to spend their time in these ways.
ex.scene: Photo 1: A peaceful beach at sunset · Photo 2: Someone hiking in the mountains

ex.t: {I suppose it's because} they'll remember seeing something new for years.
ex.q: Compare the two photographs and say what might make these travel experiences memorable for the people.
ex.scene: Photo 1: Tourists visiting famous buildings and landmarks in a city · Photo 2: Someone on an adventure in nature, by a lake in the mountains

reels.p: I would say that the main reason … is …
reels.bt: I would say that the main reason is…
reels.note: Shows you can pick out what matters most.

ex.t: {I would say that the main reason} they chose these activities {is} to relax together.
ex.q: Compare the two photographs and say why the people might have chosen to spend their time in these ways.
ex.scene: Photo 1: People watching a film in a cinema · Photo 2: A family playing a board game together at home

ex.t: {I would say that the main reason} they're outdoors {is} to escape their busy lives.
ex.q: Compare the two photographs and say why the people might have decided to spend their time in these ways.
ex.scene: Photo 1: A peaceful beach at sunset · Photo 2: Someone hiking in the mountains

ex.t: {I would say that the main reason} they're smiling {is} that they're with friends.
ex.q: Compare the two photographs and say how the people might be feeling in these situations.
ex.scene: Photo 1: A crowded city street at night, full of lights and people · Photo 2: A group of students studying together in a library

reels.note: Perfect when the question is about choosing.

ex.t: Some people prefer training alone {rather than} depending on a team.
ex.q: Compare the two photographs and say what skills the people might be developing through these activities.
ex.scene: Photo 1: A team playing football together on a field · Photo 2: Someone working out alone in a gym

ex.t: Lots of people shop at markets {rather than} malls to support local farmers.
ex.q: Compare the two photographs and say what might be enjoyable or frustrating about shopping in these places.
ex.scene: Photo 1: A big, modern shopping mall with lots of stores · Photo 2: A local market with individual stalls

ex.t: The children are learning at home {rather than} in a classroom.
ex.q: Compare the two photographs and say what the people might be learning from these experiences.
ex.scene: Photo 1: University students studying together in a library · Photo 2: A parent at home helping young children with a tablet

reels.p: In my experience, … helps you to …
reels.bt: In my experience, it helps you to…
reels.note: A personal reason sounds real and convincing.

ex.t: {In my experience,} playing in a team {helps you to} make friends quickly.
ex.q: Compare the two photographs and say what skills the people might be developing through these activities.
ex.scene: Photo 1: A team playing football together on a field · Photo 2: Someone working out alone in a gym

ex.t: {In my experience,} studying with others {helps you to} stay motivated.
ex.q: Compare the two photographs and say what the people might be learning from these experiences.
ex.scene: Photo 1: University students studying together in a library · Photo 2: A parent at home helping young children with a tablet

ex.t: {In my experience,} working in a café {helps you to} concentrate, if it's not too loud.
ex.q: Compare the two photographs and say what might be difficult for the people in these situations.
ex.scene: Photo 1: A group of colleagues in a meeting around an office table · Photo 2: Someone working alone on a laptop in a café

reels.p: One reason someone might prefer … is …
reels.bt: One reason someone might prefer this is…
reels.note: Answers from their point of view, not yours.

ex.t: {One reason someone might prefer} the market {is} that the food is fresher.
ex.q: Compare the two photographs and say what might be enjoyable or frustrating about shopping in these places.
ex.scene: Photo 1: A big, modern shopping mall with lots of stores · Photo 2: A local market with individual stalls

ex.t: {One reason someone might prefer} the café {is} that it's more relaxed than an office.
ex.q: Compare the two photographs and say what might be difficult for the people in these situations.
ex.scene: Photo 1: A group of colleagues in a meeting around an office table · Photo 2: Someone working alone on a laptop in a café

ex.t: {One reason someone might prefer} the mountains {is} that they're much quieter than a city.
ex.q: Compare the two photographs and say what might make these travel experiences memorable for the people.
ex.scene: Photo 1: Tourists visiting famous buildings and landmarks in a city · Photo 2: Someone on an adventure in nature, by a lake in the mountains

reels.note: Ends your minute with a confident opinion.

ex.t: {As far as I'm concerned,} both families are choosing time together over screens.
ex.q: Compare the two photographs and say why the people might have chosen to spend their time in these ways.
ex.scene: Photo 1: People watching a film in a cinema · Photo 2: A family playing a board game together at home

ex.t: {As far as I'm concerned,} the students in the library are probably a bit stressed.
ex.q: Compare the two photographs and say how the people might be feeling in these situations.
ex.scene: Photo 1: A crowded city street at night, full of lights and people · Photo 2: A group of students studying together in a library

ex.t: {As far as I'm concerned,} both places are perfect for switching off.
ex.q: Compare the two photographs and say why the people might have decided to spend their time in these ways.
ex.scene: Photo 1: A peaceful beach at sunset · Photo 2: Someone hiking in the mountains
